newsitem.title: USA: Klein nomination caught between two senators.
newsitem.headline: Klein nomination caught between two senators.

text.p: Joel Klein Tuesday found his nomination to head the Justice Department's antitrust division caught between two senators with opposite views about local phone company competition.

Klein has been serving as acting assistant attorney general for antitrust since the departure last year of Anne Bingaman. In that capacity, it has been his delicate responsibility to carry out Congress's wishes -- expressed in a law passed last year -- to foster a competitive market in telecommunications.

A spokesman for Sen. Ernest Hollings said through a spokesman Tuesday he had put a parliamentary hold to prevent a Senate vote on Klein, because Klein has been too permissive with phone companies that want to merge.

The South Carolina Democrat was reacting to pressure applied to Klein Sen. Conrad Burns. The Montana Republican put the nomination on "hold" because he thought Klein was dragging his heels on giving the local phone company SBC more latitude to compete in the long-distance market.

Klein is charged with the task of telling the Federal Communications Commission whether he believes local phone companies have permitted real local competition. Only once there is real local competition may local phone companies enter the long-distance market.
In an effort to accomodate Burns' concerns, Klein ran afoul of Hollings.

Hollings, who was to meet with Klein later Tuesday, was concerned that Klein permitted the $21 billion merger of Bell Atlantic Corp. and Nynex Corp. last month. And he worries about what Klein's policies may be in the future.

"Joel Klein has been misreading the Telecommunications Reform Act and until the point that Mr. Kleinn understands the law as it was passed, then Sen. Hollings will continue his hold," a spokesman for Hollings said. "The act was designed to promote competition, not consolidation."
